</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In February 2016, the FASB issued <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ASU&nbsp;2016-02,</FONT><I>&nbsp;Leases
(Topic 842)</I><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&nbsp;(&#147;ASU&nbsp;2016-02&#148;),&nbsp;which</FONT> requires lessees to recognize leases on the balance sheet and disclose key information about leasing arrangements.
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ASU&nbsp;2016-02&nbsp;establishes</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">a&nbsp;right-of-use&nbsp;model</FONT></FONT> (&#147;ROU&#148;) that requires a lessee to recognize a ROU
asset and corresponding lease liability on the balance sheet for all leases with a term longer than twelve months. Leases will be classified as finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern and classification of expense recognition
in the statement of operations. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ASU&nbsp;2016-02&nbsp;is</FONT> effective for annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted.
The Company expects to adopt <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ASU&nbsp;2016-02&nbsp;on</FONT> December&nbsp;31, 2018, which is the first day of its fiscal year 2019. A modified retrospective transition is required for leases existing at, or entered
into after, the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented in the financial statements, with certain practical expedients available. The Company expects that <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ASU&nbsp;2016-02&nbsp;will</FONT> have a
material effect on its consolidated financial statements. While the Company is continuing to assess the impact of adoption, it currently believes the most significant changes relate to (1)&nbsp;the recognition of new ROU assets and lease
</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B></B><B><I>Term Loan and Revolving Line of Credit</I></B><B> </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On October&nbsp;9, 2012,
the Company entered into a credit agreement (&#147;Credit Agreement&#148;) with several financial institutions, collateralized by all of the assets of the Company. The Credit Agreement, provided for borrowings under a term loan of
$175.0&nbsp;million and a revolving line of credit up to $25.0&nbsp;million with a maturity date of October&nbsp;9, 2017. On May&nbsp;15, 2013, the Credit Agreement was amended for an additional term loan to allow the Company to borrow an additional
$50.0&nbsp;million, the proceeds of which were used to fund a distribution to the Series A Preferred Stock stockholders of the Company. On April&nbsp;11, 2014, the Credit Agreement was amended for an additional term loan to allow the Company to
borrow an additional $50.0&nbsp;million with a maturity date on the term loan and revolver extended to October&nbsp;9, 2018, the proceeds of which were used to fund a distribution to the Series A Preferred Stock stockholders of the Company. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On July&nbsp;23, 2015, in order to permit the Merger, the Company entered into Amendment
No.&nbsp;3 to the Credit Agreement (&#147;Amendment No.&nbsp;3&#148;). Amendment No.&nbsp;3, among other things, deemed the Company (as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">successor-in-interest</FONT></FONT> to BHIH),
as of the Merger effective date, to be a party to the Credit Agreement as a &#147;Guarantor&#148; and &#147;Loan Party&#148; thereunder. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Agreement was further amended on September&nbsp;25, 2015 (&#147;Amendment No.&nbsp;4&#148;), to, among other things, extend the
maturity date on the Credit Agreement for two additional years to October&nbsp;9, 2020 and lower the Applicable Rate (as defined in Amendment No.&nbsp;4). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Agreement was further amended on October&nbsp;19, 2016 (&#147;Amendment No.&nbsp;5&#148;) to, among other things, increase allowable
indebtedness associated with capital lease obligations, synthetic lease obligations and purchase money obligations, as well as to increase allowable cash capital expenditures during each fiscal year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Agreement was further amended on December&nbsp;20, 2017 (&#147;Amendment No.&nbsp;6&#148;) to, among other things, extend the
maturity date on the Credit Agreement to December&nbsp;20, 2022 and increase the revolving line of credit from up to $25.0&nbsp;million to up to $50.0&nbsp;million. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During the term of the Credit Agreement, the Company is allowed to borrow amounts under base rate or Eurodollar rate loans. Base rate loans are
charged interest at the higher of the Bank of America&#146;s prime rate, the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.50%, or the LIBOR rate for one month loans plus 1.00% and an applicable rate. The applicable rate for base rate loans was 1.25% and 1.00% as of
December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, Bank of America&#146;s prime rate was the highest of the three rates at 4.50% as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 3.75% as of
December&nbsp;25, 2016 that resulted in a total interest rate of 5.75% and 4.75% as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, respectively. Interest on base rate loans is due on each calendar quarter end, with the same principal maturity
date as the Credit Agreement. Base rate loans may be repaid or converted to a Eurodollar rate loan at any time during the term of the Credit Agreement without penalty. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Eurodollar rate loans may be entered or converted into one, two, three, or six month periods. The Eurodollar rate loans are charged interest at
the LIBOR rate on the effective date for the period selected, plus an applicable rate. The applicable rate for Eurodollar rate loans was 2.25% and 2.00% as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31,
2017, the one, two, three, and six month LIBOR rates were 1.56%, 1.62%, 1.69%, and 1.84%, respectively. As of December&nbsp;25, 2016, the one, two, three, and six month LIBOR rates were 0.76%, 0.81%, 1.00%, and 1.32%, respectively. As the Eurodollar
rate loans mature, they may be converted into new Eurodollar rate loans, converted into base rate loans or repaid. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&nbsp;31,
2017, there were outstanding balances under the term loan in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-month</FONT> Eurodollar loans of $125.1&nbsp;million, all of which were accruing interest at a rate of approximately 3.82%. As of December&nbsp;25,
2016, there were outstanding balances under the term loan in <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-month</FONT> Eurodollar loans of $157.5&nbsp;million, all of which were accruing interest at a rate of approximately 2.61%. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, there were no outstanding balances under the revolving line of credit. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Leases </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On May&nbsp;5, 2017, the Company entered into an agreement with a financial
institution providing for up to $3.0&nbsp;million for leasing of equipment, which is scheduled to expire on June&nbsp;30, 2018. Under this leasing arrangement, each of the scheduled leases has a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">60-month</FONT> term,
a fixed interest rate equal to the average of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">two-</FONT> and three-year interest rate swap rates as published by the Bloomberg Swap report on the lease commencement date for the specific equipment project plus 300
basis points, and a bargain purchase option at the end of the lease of $1. As a result of the bargain purchase option, the Company has classified the leases under this leasing arrangement as capital leases. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On May&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company entered into an agreement with another financial institution providing for up to $10.0&nbsp;million for
leasing of equipment, which is scheduled to expire on June&nbsp;1, 2018. Under this leasing arrangement, each of the scheduled leases has a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">60-month</FONT> term, a fixed interest rate equal to the interest rate swap
for a 2.61 year weighted average life as published by the Bloomberg Swap report on the lease commencement date for the specific equipment project plus 300 basis points, and a bargain purchase option at the end of the lease of $1. As a result of the
bargain purchase option, the Company has classified the leases under this leasing arrangement as capital leases. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On October&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company&#146;s board of directors authorized a share repurchase program under which we may purchase up to
$50.0&nbsp;million of our outstanding common stock through April&nbsp;30, 2019. The purchases may be made from time to time in the open market (including, without limitation, the use of Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10b5-1</FONT> plans),
depending on a number of factors, including the Company&#146;s evaluation of general market and economic conditions, the trading price of the common stock, regulatory requirements, and compliance with the terms of the Company&#146;s outstanding
indebtedness. The share repurchase program may be extended, modified, suspended or discontinued at any time. The Company expects to fund the share repurchase program with either, or a combination of, existing cash on hand, cash generated from
operations, and borrowings under its revolving line of credit. The Company acquired 0.2&nbsp;million shares at a total cost of $2.0&nbsp;million under this program during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017. Subsequent to December&nbsp;31, 2017 and
through March&nbsp;1, 2018, the Company acquired an additional 0.2&nbsp;million shares at a total cost of </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-19 </P>

of investments held in a rabbi trust. These investments consist of money market funds and mutual funds and the fair value measurements are derived using quoted prices in active markets for the specific funds which are based on Level&nbsp;1 inputs of

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>(16)</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Income Taxes </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On December&nbsp;22, 2017 the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#147;Tax
Act&#148;) was signed into law. Among other provisions, the Tax Act reduces the federal statutory corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21%. During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017, the Company recognized a deferred income tax benefit of
$40.1&nbsp;million due to the revaluation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities to reflect the new lower rate. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Based on the
Company&#146;s current interpretation of the Tax Act, it made reasonable estimates to record provisional adjustments during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2017. The Company will continue to analyze additional information and guidance related to the
Tax Act as supplemental legislation, regulatory guidance, changes in accounting standards, or evolving technical interpretations become available. The final impacts may result in an adjustment to the $40.1&nbsp;million benefit recorded during the
fourth quarter of fiscal 2017, and the Company will continue to refine such amounts within the measurement period provided by the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;). The Company expects to complete its analysis no later than the
fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B><I>Concentration of Interest Rate Risk</I></B> </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest rate risk is the exposure to loss
resulting from changes in the level of interest rates and the spread between different interest rates. Interest rate risk is highly sensitive due to many factors, including U.S. monetary and tax policies, U.S. and international economic factors and
other factors beyond our control. The Company&#146;s credit facility has floating interest rates. The Company is exposed to changes in the level of interest rates and to changes in the relationship or spread between interest rates for our floating
rate debt. The Company&#146;s floating rate debt will require payments based on a variable interest rate index such as LIBOR. Therefore, increases in interest rates may reduce the Company&#146;s net income by increasing the cost
</P>

of the Company&#146;s debt. However, the Company seeks to mitigate some of its floating interest rate risk on long-term debt by entering into fixed pay interest rate derivatives on a portion of
our outstanding long-term debt (see Note 2). </P> <P STYLE="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B><I>Concentration of Credit Risk</I></B> </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Certain financial instruments potentially subject
the Company to a concentration of credit risk. These financial instruments consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents and accounts and vendor receivables. The Company places its cash and cash equivalents with high-credit, quality financial
institutions. At times, the balances in the accounts exceed the amounts insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Concentration of credit risk with respect to receivables is primarily limited to franchisees, which are primarily located in the southeastern
United States and certain vendors. Royalty revenues from three franchisees, one of which is a related party franchisee, accounted for approximately 44% of the Company&#146;s total franchise royalty revenues for each of the fiscal years ended
December&nbsp;31, 2017, December&nbsp;25, 2016 and December&nbsp;27, 2015, respectively. Royalty and franchise fee accounts receivable from three franchisees, one of which is a related party franchisee, accounted for approximately 42% and 40% of the
Company&#146;s gross royalty and franchise fee accounts receivable as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, respectively. The Company continually evaluates and monitors the credit history of its franchisees and believes it has an
adequate allowance for bad debts. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">(d)</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B><I>Concentration of Commodity Price Risk</I></B> </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company purchases certain products
that are affected by commodity prices and are, therefore, subject to price volatility caused by weather, market conditions and other factors which are not considered predictable or within our control. Although these products are subject to changes
in commodity prices, certain purchasing contracts or pricing arrangements contain risk management techniques designed to minimize price volatility. The purchasing contracts and pricing arrangements we use may result in unconditional purchase
obligations, which are not reflected in our consolidated balance sheets. Typically, the Company uses these types of purchasing techniques to control costs as an alternative to directly managing financial instruments to hedge commodity prices. In
many cases, the Company believes it will be able to address material commodity cost increases by adjusting our menu pricing, promotional mix, or changing our product delivery strategy. However, increases in commodity prices, without adjustments to
our menu prices, could increase food and supplies costs as a percentage of company-operated restaurant revenues and customers may react negatively to increases in our menu prices which could adversely impact customer traffic and revenues. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">(e)</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B><I>Sponsorships</I></B> </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has entered into various sponsorship agreements with
original terms of up to ten years to receive certain advertising rights, the use of certain advertising territories, and vendor products as defined in the agreements. These amounts are reflected as operating costs within Company-operated restaurant
operating expenses in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income, generally in the year in which the amounts are incurred. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">F-27 </P>

</DIV></Center>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B><I>Deferred Compensation Plan</I></B> </TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has a rabbi trust to invest compensation
deferred under our nonqualified deferred compensation plan and fund future deferred compensation obligations. The rabbi trust is subject to creditor claims in the event of insolvency, but the assets held in the rabbi trust are not available for
general corporate purposes. This plan allows eligible participants to defer compensation. Deferred compensation, net of accumulated earnings and/or losses on the participant-directed investment options, is distributable in cash at employee specified
dates or upon retirement, death, disability or termination from the plan. Realized and unrealized gains and losses on these securities are recorded in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income and offset changes in deferred
compensation liabilities to participants. The assets of the plan were $2.5&nbsp;million and $3.1&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016, respectively, and are subject to the Company&#146;s creditors and are included in
the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><B>Stock Compensation Plan </B></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under the Amended and Restated 2011 Equity Incentive Plan (the
&#147;Amended 2011 Plan&#148;), the Company&#146;s board of directors may grant stock options, restricted stock units and performance awards to officers, directors, employees, and consultants of the Company and its subsidiaries. There are up to
8.5&nbsp;million shares available for issuance under the Amended 2011 Plan of authorized but unissued common stock. At December&nbsp;31, 2017, there were 3.7&nbsp;million additional shares available for grant under the Amended 2011 Plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Stock Options </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Stock options are granted at a price determined by the board of directors or committee designated by the board at not less than the fair market
value of a share on the date of grant. The term of each option shall be determined by the board of directors or committee designated by the board at the time of grant and shall be no greater than ten&nbsp;years. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes-Merton option-pricing model. No dividends are
expected to be paid over the contractual term of the stock options granted, resulting in the use of a zero expected dividend rate. Volatility was estimated based on the average historical volatility of similar entities with publicly traded shares.
The expected term for options granted is derived using the &#147;simplified&#148; method, in accordance with SEC guidance. The risk-free rate for the expected term of the option is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve at the date of grant. There
were no stock options granted during the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;27, 2015. The assumptions used for grants made during the fiscal years ended December&nbsp;31, 2017 and December&nbsp;25, 2016 are provided in the following table: </P>
